Reconvene to Regular Session / Roll Call / Report Out on Closed Session
Welcome by the School Board President, Mike Wells
Changes to the Agenda
Approval of Agenda
Oral Communication

publicComments.name: Finbar Rafferty
publicComments.summary: A 3rd-grade Orion student with a disability described his experience taking an online college paleoanthropology class and asked the district to provide more advanced and challenging coursework in school.

publicComments.name: Megan O'Reilly Green
publicComments.summary: Advocated for changes to board policy 5123 to explicitly support academic acceleration for high-ability students, citing research, equity concerns, and the risk of losing families to private schools without advanced options at middle school.

publicComments.name: Sirsha
publicComments.summary: An incoming Kennedy student who scored at the 97th percentile for 8th graders on i-Ready described her experience with ADHD and argued that advanced coursework at Kennedy is essential for students who need ongoing challenge to make progress.

publicComments.name: Elmer Molina
publicComments.summary: A KIPP Excelencia parent asked the board to prioritize air conditioning at the school, describing seeing his children and others visibly overheated when he picks them up.

publicComments.name: Jose Talavera
publicComments.summary: The KIPP Associate Director of Advocacy asked the board to include KIPP Excelencia campus upgrades (including AC) in the facility master plan discussion at the April 23 study session, and invited trustees to a campus tree-planting event on Monday.

publicComments.name: Carmen Flores
publicComments.summary: A KIPP Excelencia parent of two girls asked the board to include KIPP Excelencia in the facilities master plan budget, citing concerns about heat and water quality at the school.

publicComments.name: Juan Bale
publicComments.summary: A KIPP Excelencia parent congratulated Hoover on its improvements and asked the board to also consider KIPP Excelencia for facility improvements including classrooms and the playground area.

publicComments.name: Chris Terry
publicComments.summary: An Orion parent praised the district's equity efforts but urged the board to provide advanced coursework at Kennedy Middle School so that students who don't attend North Star have equitable access to challenging classes, noting that wealthier families supplement with expensive private tutoring.

publicComments.name: Pam Barash
publicComments.summary: A 23-year Henry Ford kindergarten teacher raised two concerns: that the newly installed temporary AC units are disruptive, noisy, and not conducive to classroom learning, and that kindergarten teachers are losing their traditional minimum-day assessment period at the start of the school year.

publicComments.name: May
publicComments.summary: A professional mathematician and Orion parent advocated for policy changes to increase access to advanced middle school curriculum, arguing that without differentiated courses, public schools fail their equity mission and leave high-ability students from lower-income families behind.
